summary: The segmenter tends to place boundaries right at causal/conditional connectives (-다보니까, -아서, -고) that still bind the following clause grammatically or semantically, producing verbless fragments, duplicated discourse markers, or mood shifts. Conversely, on longer multi-clause sentences with clear punctuation or temporal-clause boundaries it often segments nothing at all, sacrificing latency gains for no quality benefit. The core fix is boundary selection tied to clause completeness rather than mere token position.
